Incorporating the Beige Book alongside the January 29, 2020 FOMC statement reinforces a modestly dovish read. The Beige Book points to modest overall growth, strong but tight labor markets, and muted price pressures, while noting softness in manufacturing/trade-exposed sectors and pockets of weakness in energy. Importantly for the outlook, District contacts reported tighter lending standards and weaker demand in credit-sensitive areas such as construction and land development, aligning with SLOOS evidence of banks tightening C&I and CRE terms, raising credit score thresholds, and reducing risk tolerance. Combined with the Financial Stability Report’s caution on leverage and stretched valuations, these insights suggest rising headwinds to capex and credit-sensitive activity, validating a stay-on-hold stance with a risk-management (dovish) bias. Net effect: the otherwise constructive macro tone is tempered by tightening credit conditions and softer loan demand, nudging sentiment lower.
